First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(2{n}^{2}-3)(2{n}^{2}+3)}{{n}^{2}(5-12{n}^{3})}=\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{5{n}^{2}-12{n}^{5}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{5{n}^{2}-12{n}^{5}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-12{n}^{5},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{4{n}^{4}-9}{5{n}^{2}-12{n}^{5}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4{n}^{4}}{{n}^{5}}-\frac{9}{{n}^{5}})}{(\frac{5{n}^{2}}{{n}^{5}}-\frac{12{n}^{5}}{{n}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4}{n}-\frac{9}{{n}^{5}})}{(\frac{5}{{n}^{3}}-12)} \\  & =\frac{0-0}{0-12} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $0.$
